merged.title: xs-rs performance: beat xs-c++ on congress-sample update-10pct
merged.summary: xs-rs now packs small DATA records across directory NEEDs instead of flushing one tiny DATA frame per NEED, and automatic compression no longer spends zstd on kilobyte-sized listings. On a 2-CPU, 11 ms-RTT race of the congress-sample update-10pct shape it improved from 1.61 s to 1.43 s against the parent binary, with CPU down about 13%. Explicit -z still compresses every listing as before.

merged.title: xs-rs performance: beat xs-c++ on congress-sample update-10pct
merged.summary: The change makes the xs-rs sender behave like xs-c++ at two points on the update path: it flushes a partial DATA block when its worker goes idle, and automatic compression can no longer escalate to zstd level 6 after a transient writer stall. Local update-10pct races were already ahead of xs-c++ and stayed within noise, but the change targets the lab's slow block, where xs-rs sent 5.75 MB instead of 7.54 MB and burned more CPU, consistent with a level-6 feedback stall.

agent.summary: Split the 1,396-line `transfer.rs` into responsibility-based modules: `sender.rs` (walk/read/DATA engine), `outbox.rs` (writer thread and frame queue), and `event.rs` (receiver output events and progress acknowledgments), leaving `transfer.rs` as the shared root. Also shared the duplicated CHUNK record encoder between the ranged and sequential read paths, and logged the two merged performance steps plus these cleanups in README.md. No behavior or wire bytes changed.
agent.diagnosis: This was structural debt rather than a runtime hot path: the recent batching and idle-flush steps had grown `transfer.rs` to 1,396 lines mixing three jobs (sender engine, writer/queue, receiver event helpers). Baseline and post-change measurements were the four gates: 144 tests pass (31 xs-rs unit, 74 xs-rs integration, 31 xs-wire unit, 8 xs-wire integration), clippy `-D warnings` clean, rustfmt clean, and the aarch64 cross-check clean. Diffing each moved section against the original shows only visibility keywords changed, plus the CHUNK helper dedup.
agent.change:
- `transfer/sender.rs`: sender engine, `AUTO_LISTING_MIN`, `DATA_BATCH`, walk/read workers, `run_sender`, `read_replies`, and a single `chunk_record` helper used by both read paths.
- `transfer/outbox.rs`: `Queue`/`Outbox`, `FrameOut`, `FrameTx`, `write_observed`, `link_now`, `send_fatal`, and `MAX_QUEUED`.
- `transfer/event.rs`: `report_event`, `progress_ack`, `taken_event`, `directory_event`, `transferred_code`, `metadata_code`.
- `transfer.rs`: now only `msg_code`, module declarations and the `run_sender`/`run_receiver` re-exports.
- Updated imports in `receiver.rs`, `receiver/data.rs`, `receiver/dir.rs`, `hardlink.rs`.
- Added the 2026-10-22 changelog entry with the two merged steps and two cleanup lines.
agent.expected_effect: No change to transfer behavior or wire output; the sender, writer, and receiver event code now live in files named for their responsibility, and the CHUNK record layout is encoded in one place. This should make future changes to the batching/idle-flush logic easier to locate and review.
agent.risks: The split is a pure move; visibility was widened only to `pub(super)` within the `transfer` subtree, and submodule imports were updated. The CHUNK helper preserves the exact field order and resume-prefix condition (`resume.then_some(prefix.size)`), so encoded bytes are identical. Full test suite plus clippy/fmt/aarch64 checks pass.
